_note: Solar ATAP (GP/ST/No.60/2025) covers TNB's jurisdiction only — Peninsular Malaysia + Labuan. Sabah (SESB) and Sarawak (SESCO/Sarawak Energy) run their own separate net-metering schemes, not Solar ATAP. See app/services/solar_calc.py for which fields apply where.

sesb._source: SESB average base domestic tariff, revised 1 Feb 2026 (sesb.com.my). SESB publishes a block schedule we could not machine-read reliably as of this update — using the published average rate as a single flat approximation. Verify exact block rates at sesb.com.my before quoting a customer.
sesb.export_note: SESB runs its own Net Energy Metering (NEM) scheme, separate from Solar ATAP. Exported electricity nets against consumption at the prevailing domestic rate (no separate published feed-in/export tariff found) — modelled here as 1:1 net metering at the flat domestic rate.

sesco._source: Sarawak Energy domestic tariff block table (sarawakenergy.com), stepped-average design: total monthly consumption falling in a bracket is billed at that bracket's flat rate for all units. A temporary 25% domestic discount was announced for Apr-Dec 2026 — NOT applied here. Verify current rate/discount status at sarawakenergy.com before quoting a customer.
sesco.nemss_subsidy_note: Sarawak Energy also offers a one-off NEM Subsidy Scheme (NEMSS) toward install cost: RM8,000 (2-3.5kWac), RM10,000 (>3.5-6kWac), RM12,000 (>6-50kWac) — a capital subsidy, not an export tariff.
sesco.export_note: Sarawak Energy's NEM nets exported electricity against consumption at the prevailing domestic rate (no separate published feed-in/export tariff found) — modelled here as 1:1 net metering at the applicable bracket rate.
